title: Liouville Energy and the Rightmost Zeta Zero
description: The sliding-window energy Q(N) of the Liouville function grows like N^(2Θ), where Θ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. We prove that Q(N) exceeds N^(2σ) for all large N whenever σ < Θ, so that a bound along one infinite sequence already locates Θ; that changing the Liouville function on primes of size x^β can break the exponent when β > 1/2 and cannot when β ≤ 1/2; an endpoint form of the Nyman–Beurling criterion in weighted norms; and explicit unconditional bounds, including |L(x)| ≤ x/2641 + 8.3√x. The archive contains the paper, a Lean 4 project (21 theorems) and three Julia programs. The Riemann hypothesis is not proved.
